title: contar (cuento), contar con, espero que, vean, the personal a, al

cards.title: contar = to count / to tell (a story)
cards.body: Like English 'recount'. Cuento = I tell, and un cuento = a story.

examples.en: I want you to tell me.
I want you (all) to tell me something.

cards.title: contar con = to count on
cards.body: Spanish says 'count with'. Spanish speakers saying 'count with me' in English is a clue.

examples.en: I want you to count on me.
I hope you can count on me.
We hope they tell it to María.
examples.es: Esperamos que lo cuenten a María.

cards.title: ver → vea (from veo)
cards.body: Swapping ven would give 'van' (they go), so the mood tense builds on veo: vea, vean.

cards.title: The personal a
cards.body: When a specific person receives the action (and no other preposition is there), add a. Word order is flexible, so without it 'comprenda David' would mean 'David understands'.

examples.en: I want him to see the man.
I want the man to see.

cards.title: me gusta que + mood tense
cards.body: The personal a is for specific people (find THE plumber vs A plumber). It can also personify things (escapar a la muerte).

examples.en: I like that the teacher visits.
examples.es: Me gusta que la profesora visite.

examples.en: I like that he visits the teacher.
examples.es: Me gusta que visite a la profesora.

practice.en: I want you (informal) to tell me something.
I want you (informal) to count on me.
We hope they count on María.
I want him to see the man.
I want the man to see.
practice.why: No a — the man does the seeing.

practice.en: I like that the teacher visits.
es: Me gusta que la profesora visite
Me gusta que el profesor visite
Me gusta que visite la profesora

practice.en: I like that he visits the teacher.
es: Me gusta que visite a la profesora
Me gusta que visite al profesor
